relation: oversight runs through people, and AI shapes their judgment
note: Anthropic RCT (full paper 'Who's Aligned to Whom?' read 2 Nov 2026, pp. 1-14 incl. complete limitations; appendices unread): 50 causal-inference practitioners (61 completed; 11 no-AI comparison; recruited via a paid expert-annotator marketplace); the agent's lean on four analytical decisions was randomised by coin flip. Participants went with the lean '86% of the time' (50% by chance) — random assignment identifies the lean's AVERAGE causal effect; when the agent voiced the opposite lean after a participant had taken a side (23% of decisions), they switched 60% of the time (self-selected subset); 77% repeated the agent's talking points, sometimes nearly verbatim, and only 15% mentioned the agent. PAPER'S OWN CAVEATS: the 82% recommendation-prediction figure is exploratory and in-sample (61% majority baseline, AUC 0.84); the system prompt AMPLIFIES an existing tendency ('Whether the flip rates hold for a stock agent depends on whether it has a preference on a given decision and volunteers it'); one task/domain/pinned agent (Claude Code, Opus 4.8), participants new to the domain; average effects only. Provider-authored, not independently replicated — the edge claim is the experimental finding, not a general fact about all oversight.
